summary: This invited survey reviews how Fortran programs with user-specified data distributions can be compiled into SPMD message-passing code for distributed-memory machines. It presents a four-phase translation strategy, overlap-based and aggregate communication optimizations, and inspector-executor techniques for irregular accesses, and then surveys the systems that implement them.
why_read: It is a compact early account of how distribution-based compilers turn a global-address Fortran program into message-passing code.
main_contribution: A structured description of the phases, communication primitives and optimizations for compiling distribution-annotated Fortran to message passing, together with a survey of contemporary systems.
main_limitation: The paper reports no experiments of its own and states that parallelizing compilers often need user assistance.
